What the numbers say

For the session of Thursday, October 22, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (26 US-listed stocks and ETFs on DappGo's reviewed watchlist) as neutral. SPY is below its 50-day average and above its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is sideways and realised volatility is in the calm band.

10 of 26 tickers (38%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 17 of 25 (68%) above their 200-day average. That sits between the model's 30% and 55% breadth thresholds, so breadth alone decides nothing here. On the day 11 rose and 15 fell; the median move was −2.48%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Healthcare had the strongest average move at +2.73% and Technology the weakest at −5.19%, a spread of 7.92 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 3.84 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

No ticker has a 14-day RSI at or below 30, and 3 at or above 70 (COST, SHEL, UNH). An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-10-21), the share of tickers above the 20-day average moved from 54% to 38%, and the regime reading stayed neutral.
